term: theological formulation, religious-life role and normative grammar
definition: RoleProfile distinguishes theological content and a role in first-order religious life on the same existing Practice moves. Defined and OwnStandard retain their old meanings. Describing a move as theological does not itself say whether the practice endorses it; TheologyExcludedFromOwnStandards is a separate substantive proposition.
note: Unattributed analyst reconstruction. First-order religious life is a practical role, not a first-order-logic quantifier category; a doctrinal sentence can function as confession, so role labels need not be disjoint. The old raw theology-not-grammar reply and all source/support claims remain unchanged. Existing CasedPractice.InOrdinaryUse concerns ordinary-practitioner uptake and grammar-fixing cases, whereas this profile separates content and practical role without choosing who fixes grammar or making uptake determine norms; no identification is asserted and naming fields are not needed. Actual Defined and ordinary-life endorsement witnesses prevent vacuous controls. Named uniform status coverage stays open; mixed defined moves are a precise relevant remainder. Real-world applicability and any stronger exclusive account of theological/grammatical roles remain open.
